newsitem.title: USA: S&P sees Northeast growing, but slower than U.S..
newsitem.headline: S&P sees Northeast growing, but slower than U.S..

text.p: Economic trends in the Northeast will continue to be positive in 1997, but not as strong as in the nation as a whole, Standard & Poor's Corp said on Monday.
Last year, upgrades of credit ratings in the New England and Middle Atlantic states outpaced downgrades by a ratio of three to two, less dramatic than the nationwide pace of three to one, S&P said.

"Many ratings were upgraded due to improving financial performance, as municipal entities have adjusted to operating under slower growth scenarios," the agency said in Monday's edition of CreditWeek Municipal.
Despite the good news for most areas, New York State experienced more rating downgrades than upgrades across every sector.

"New York has the weakest economic profile of all the Middle Atlantic states," S&P said. "Faced with the slowest employment growth prospects and a high tax environment, its municipalities are at the greatest risk of credit deterioration."
S&P said the state faces slow employment and income growth which strain debt and fiscal operations.

New England, on the other hand, has been growing at about the same rate as the rest of the nation. Of particular note, S&P pointed to the upgrade last year of Massachusetts Institute of Technology, which moved to AAA from AA-plus.
"This rating change also represented the first time in almost a decade that a higher educaiton institution had its debt rating raised to AAA," S&P said.
